He played in the [[National Basketball Association]] for the [[Seattle SuperSonics]] / [[Oklahoma City Thunder]] from 2004 through 2009, for the Seattle Aviators and [[Snohomish County Explosion]] of the [[National Athletic Basketball League]] in 2010, and for the [[Tokyo Apache]] of the [[bj League]] in 2010–11. He stands at {{convert|7|ft|1|in}} and played the [[Center (basketball)|center]] position. ==High school== Swift caught the attention of NBA and college scouts while playing for [[Garces Memorial High School]], and then later as the centerpiece of the [[Bakersfield High School]] team.{{Cite web |date=2016-09-21 |title=Out From The Darkness: Robert Swift's road from NBA lottery pick to drug addict to... |url=https://www.si.com/nba/2016/09/21/robert-swift-nba-drug-addiction-thunder-sonics |access-date=2025-02-23 |website=SI |language=en-US}}{{Cite web |last=Beene |first=Richard |title=Former Bakersfield High Driller and Seattle Super Sonic Robert Swift arrested on robbery charges in Seattle, and my pick eatery of the week goes to the newly remodeled Pyrenees Cafe |url=http://www.bakersfieldobserved.com/2015/01/former-bakersfield-high-driller-and.html |access-date=2025-02-23 |language=en}} During his time at Garces, the small Catholic high school broke into the ''[[USA Today]]'' top-25 high school basketball team rankings. Between his junior and senior years, Swift transferred from Garces to [[Highland High School (Bakersfield, California)|Highland High School]], and then just before his senior year, he transferred to Bakersfield High School. This move provoked a hearing by the [[California Interscholastic Federation]] that initially declared Swift ineligible for the 2003–04 season; however, this ruling was later overturned and he played his senior season.{{cite news|first=Matt |last=Hurst |url=http://www.kingdomofthesun.net/bakersfield.com%20%20Sports%20%20High%20School.htm |title=Swift happy to focus on hoops |work=[[The Bakersfield Californian]] |date=November 26, 2003 |access-date=June 12, 2006 |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20050324000808/http://www.kingdomofthesun.net/bakersfield.com%20%20Sports%20%20High%20School.htm |archive-date=March 24, 2005 }} He committed to attend the [[University of Southern California]] (USC) to play for the [[USC Trojans men's basketball]] team on a scholarship. ==National Basketball Association== Swift was selected by the [[Seattle SuperSonics]] in the first round with the twelfth overall pick in the [[2004 NBA draft]].{{cite news |last=Ikeda |first=Jordan |title=7-foot center Robert Swift opens up about his team, his uncles and his NBA future. |date=January 31, 2009 |newspaper=[[The Rafu Shimpo]] |url=http://www.rafu.com/en/2009/0131/sports.html |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20120214232510/http://www.rafu.com/en/2009/0131/sports.html |archive-date=February 14, 2012 |url-status=dead |df=mdy-all }}{{cite news | last = Allen | first = Percy | title = Robert Swift: "This is who I am" | newspaper = The Seattle Times | date = October 9, 2006 | url = http://seattletimes.nwsource.com/html/sports/2003295522_soni09.html | access-date = August 30, 2010 | quote = Swift talks about learning the language, partly because his father is half Japanese, and he has a strong desire to visit extended family members who live in Okinawa, Japan.}} Swift bypassed college and opted for the NBA, turning down his commitment to play for USC. In his first season with the Sonics, Swift played in 16 games, averaging 4.5 minutes, 0.9 points, 0.4 rebounds, and 0.4 blocks per game. In his second season, under the direction of coach [[Bob Hill]], he started 20 out of 47 games, averaging 21 minutes, 6.4 points, 5.6 rebounds, and 1.2 blocks per game. In 2006, the Sonics anticipated that Swift would become their starting center. Swift was awarded the starting job at center but he ruptured the [[anterior cruciate ligament]] in his right knee after playing just over one minute in a preseason game vs the [[Sacramento Kings]]. The resulting injury occurred when he twisted his right knee when he fell and went out of bounds awkwardly in front of the Seattle bench.[https://web.archive.org/web/20061103211246/http://sports.espn.go.com/nba/recap?gameId=261025025 Swift hurts knee, Watson loses teeth, but Sonics win], October 25, 2006 Swift suffered another injury to his right knee in February 2008, a torn [[lateral meniscus]].{{cite web |url=http://basketboltr.net/2008/02/29/robert-swift-out-for-season/ |title=Robert Swift out for season |publisher=Basketboltr.net |access-date=May 30, 2014 |url-status=usurped |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20101006074953/http://basketboltr.net/2008/02/29/robert-swift-out-for-season/ |archive-date=October 6, 2010 |df=mdy-all }} Swift's final NBA game was played on April 13, 2009, in an 83–113 loss to the [[Portland Trail Blazers]] where he recorded 2 points, 3 rebounds and 2 blocks. On December 22, 2009, the [[Oklahoma City Thunder]] renounced the rights to Swift. ==D-League and Japan== In 2009, Swift joined the [[Bakersfield Jam]] of the [[NBA D-League]].{{cite web |url=http://www.bakersfield.com/news/local/x239122641/Home-again |title=Robert Swift: Home again |publisher=Bakersfield.com |access-date=May 30, 2014 |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20150923181816/http://www.bakersfield.com/news/local/x239122641/Home-again |archive-date=September 23, 2015 |df=mdy-all }} However, he left the team for personal reasons after appearing in two games. He was overweight and experienced a decrease in mobility. During the 2010–11 season, Swift played for Tokyo Apache with his former head coach in [[Seattle SuperSonics|Seattle]], [[Bob Hill]]. Swift played well, receiving interest from the NBA's [[Boston Celtics]] and [[New York Knicks]]. Following the [[2011 Tōhoku earthquake and tsunami]], the Apache ended their season prematurely and disbanded.{{cite web|url=http://seattletimes.com/html/sports/2023691379_robertswift18xml.html?syndication=rss|title=Flameout: Young Sonics phenom Robert Swift falls hard|work=The Seattle Times|access-date=November 14, 2014}} Swift tried out for the [[Portland Trail Blazers]] in April 2011, but was not offered a contract. ==Spain== On 12 February 2018, Swift returned to play basketball after agreeing a two-year contract with Spanish [[Primera División de Baloncesto|fifth tier]] club [[Círculo Gijón]].{{cite web|url=https://www.circulobaloncestoyconocimiento.com/2018/02/12/circulo-gijon-baloncesto-ficha-nba-robert-swift/|publisher=Círculo Gijón Baloncesto y Conocimiento|language=es|title=El Círculo Gijón Baloncesto incorpora al ex NBA Robert Swift|trans-title=Círculo Gijón Baloncesto adds former NBA player Robert Swift|date=12 February 2018|access-date=12 February 2018|archive-date=February 13, 2018|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180213022146/https://www.circulobaloncestoyconocimiento.com/2018/02/12/circulo-gijon-baloncesto-ficha-nba-robert-swift/|url-status=dead}} In his second season in Spain, the club achieved a vacant place in the professional third-tier league, [[LEB Plata]]. He left the team after the end of the season averaging 9.1 points and 4.8 rebounds per game. However, Swift came back to Círculo Gijón on 29 December 2019.{{cite web|url=https://www.elcomercio.es/deportes/baloncesto/swift-regresa-circulo-20191229012434-ntvo.html|publisher=[[El comercio (Spain)|El Comercio]]|language=es|title=Swift regresa al Círculo Gijón|trans-title=Swift comes back to Círculo Gijón|date=29 December 2019}} ==Personal life== Robert's father, Bruce, was unable to work for two years due to a car accident that occurred while Robert was a child. He filed for [[bankruptcy]] twice: in 1999 and 2003. Robert's mother, Rhonda, was diagnosed with cancer and had multiple surgeries to remove it. The Swifts dealt with [[food insecurity]]. In 2009, Swift's girlfriend became pregnant. In June 2011, Swift was arrested for [[driving under the influence]]. He was found guilty of [[reckless driving]]. In 2013, Swift refused to vacate his foreclosed home, which had been bought by a new owner. The new owner bought the house in [[Sammamish, Washington]], in January 2013 for half the price Swift paid in 2006.{{cite web|last=Dwyer |first=Kelly |url=https://sports.yahoo.com/blogs/nba-ball-dont-lie/robert-swift-refusing-abandon-bullet-ridden-beer-strewn-170507711--nba.html |title=Robert Swift is refusing to abandon his bullet-ridden, beer can-strewn foreclosed house |publisher=Sports.yahoo.com |date=February 22, 2013 |access-date=May 30, 2014}}{{cite web|author=Graham Wood |url=http://realestate.aol.com/blog/2013/02/24/robert-swift-seattle-supersonics-foreclosure-eviction/ |title=Robert Swift, Ex-Seattle SuperSonics Star, Refuses to Leave His Foreclosed Home | AOL Real Estate |publisher=Realestate.aol.com |date=February 24, 2013 |access-date=May 30, 2014}} Swift eventually left the home, which was reportedly riddled with animal feces, guns, bullets, beer bottles, and garbage. Observers also noted old letters from some of the top college basketball programs in the country trying to recruit Swift, before he went straight to the NBA from high school.{{cite news| url=http://www.seattlepi.com/local/komo/article/Former-Sonic-s-foreclosed-home-bullets-feces-4329299.php | work=Seattle Post-Intelligencer | first1=Jon | last1=Humbert | title=Former Sonic's foreclosed home: bullets, feces, stink | date=March 5, 2013}} In October 2014, police raided the house of Trygve Bjorkstam, an alleged heroin and methamphetamine dealer, who had a collection of 18 guns. They found Swift living in the home, and in possession of a sawed-off shotgun. In November 2014, police charged Swift with unlawful possession of a short-barreled shotgun.{{cite web|url=http://www.seattlepi.com/local/article/Ex-Seattle-Sonic-Robert-Swift-charged-after-5888804.php|title=Ex-Seattle Sonic Robert Swift charged after police seize grenade launcher, drugs from Kirkland home|work=seattlepi.com|date=November 12, 2014|access-date=November 14, 2014}} On January 8, 2015, Swift was arrested by police for involvement in an armed home invasion attempt. Swift claimed he was high on drugs at the time of the incident.{{cite web |url=http://www.kirotv.com/news/news/former-sonic-arrested-home-invasion-robbery-plot/njjqW/ |title=Former Sonic arrested in
